name: Unifiram

lead: Unifiram is an experimental nootropic from Italian labs, sold online. Sunifiram is derived from it.
No source links it to appearance.

paras: Mechanism unknown; indirect AMPA pathway involvement has been suggested.
No human or long-term toxicity studies exist.

lead: Unifiram (DM-232) is an experimental compound that showed antiamnesic effects in animal studies, with far greater potency than piracetam. It was developed by Italian researchers and is the parent of sunifiram.[1][2] It is not patented and is sold online despite the absence of human and long-term toxicity studies.[1][3]
Sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

paras: Unifiram and sunifiram showed no affinity for tested receptors, channels or transporters up to 1 micromolar and did not potentiate recombinant AMPA receptors, but prevented amnesia caused by an AMPA antagonist.[2][4] The (R)-(+) enantiomer is the more active.[1]
No studies found. A 2022 review of nootropics in healthy individuals covers the category generally.[5]
